html:
The Palace of Nations in Geneva was built from 1929 to 1936 as the headquarters of the League of Nations. It now houses the United Nations office in Geneva.

The League had sat in Geneva since 1920, because Swiss neutrality made the city acceptable to all. Its grand new home was finished just as the League failed to stop Italy in Ethiopia and Japan in China, and it stood almost empty through the Second World War.

The United Nations took it over in 1946. It hosts more meetings than any other UN site: human rights, disarmament and peace talks. With the Red Cross and the World Health Organization nearby, it made Geneva a capital of diplomacy.
